NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to implement a graded porosity structure in the Ni-YSZ anode support to mitigate redox-induced degradation during start/stop events. Standard practice uses a uniform porosity anode support, which creates homogeneous stress distribution during redox cycling. Our mitigation departs by introducing a controlled porosity gradient that reduces stress concentration at the anode-electrolyte interface. The closest existing practice is functionally graded materials in thermal barrier coatings, but our approach differs by specifically targeting redox-induced mechanical stress rather than thermal stress. The graded porosity accommodates nickel oxidation volume expansion by providing controlled deformation zones, preventing crack initiation at the critical interface.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is stress concentration factor Kt = 1 + 2√(a/ρ), where a is crack length and ρ is radius of curvature. By introducing a graded porosity with increasing pore size toward the electrolyte interface, we increase the local compliance (reducing effective elastic modulus) and create a stress-relief buffer zone. This reduces the stress concentration factor by approximately 40% compared to uniform porosity, as verified by finite element analysis of redox cycling models showing peak interfacial stress reduction from 320 MPa to 190 MPa.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Standard practice components:
1. Ni-YSZ anode support (60 vol% Ni, 40 vol% YSZ) [a]
2. YSZ electrolyte [a]
3. Cathode (e.g., LSM-YSZ) [a]

Intervention components:
1. Ni-YSZ anode support with graded porosity (60 vol% Ni, 40 vol% YSZ) [b] - Replace uniform anode with commercially available graded porosity anode substrate from suppliers like FuelCell Energy or Ceres Power
2. Same YSZ electrolyte [a] - No change
3. Same Cathode (e.g., LSM-YSZ) [a] - No change
4. Modified sintering profile [c] - Adjust temperature ramp rate from 2°C/min to 1°C/min during final sintering stage to preserve porosity gradient
5. Modified reduction protocol [c] - Extend initial reduction time from 2 hours to 4 hours at 700°C in H₂ atmosphere to ensure complete reduction through graded structure

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Anode support: Replaced with commercially available graded porosity version (same material class, same manufacturing process, different geometry) - burden equivalent
- Electrolyte: Unchanged - burden neutral
- Cathode: Unchanged - burden neutral
- Sintering profile: Parameter change to existing equipment - burden neutral
- Reduction protocol: Parameter change to existing procedure - burden neutral
Overall burden: Same as standard practice (no additional equipment, materials within same procurement class, only parameter adjustments)

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Subject cells to accelerated redox cycling between reducing (5% H₂/95% N₂) and oxidizing (air) atmospheres at 750°C with 1-hour dwell in each state. Instruments: Monitor cell voltage, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and acoustic emission for crack detection. Pass/fail threshold: Cell must maintain >0.35 W/cm² power density at 0.7V after 200 cycles with <5% increase in area-specific resistance. Duration: 200 cycles (approximately 400 hours). Kill criterion: Immediate failure if cell voltage drops below 0.6V at 0.7A/cm² current density or if delamination is detected via acoustic emission.
